physicalQuestion: Can a basketball impact make one bottle cap detach through a Blender Bullet breakable fixed constraint while every post-release body transform, the break response, the shot frames and the final poses remain solver-owned?
directVisualQuestions: Does the cause frame show a recognizable basketball, three readable bottles and an attached cap before impact?
Is the basketball-to-bottle contact continuous without an obvious gap or penetration?
Does the cap remain visibly attached before the measured primary contact?
Does cap separation begin only after the collision and remain causally readable?
Does the cap follow one continuous trajectory without teleporting or a hand-authored-looking jump?
Does the detached object still read at bottle-cap scale with recognizable cap material and shape?
Do at least two bottles respond continuously while their final poses remain visibly unstaged?
Does the secondary response add physical richness without becoming an explosive or chaotic effect?
Does the derived effect shot include the response bottles and detached cap with useful occupancy?
Do the court lighting, enclosure, material readability and shot progression still feel filmic without fake debris, particles or camera shake?
forbiddenSubstitutions: manual kinematic or transform key at a break frame
typed detachment time, detached pose, landing pose or detachment velocity
particles, debris sprites, dust, camera shake or sound used as evidence of breakage
postprocess blur used to conceal discontinuity
fracture, deformation, liquid-slosh or material-failure claim from this cap-attachment experiment
weaker RC4 primary collision, solver ownership, exact reopen or visual thresholds
threshold weakening after inspecting the result
claimCeiling: One Blender Bullet breakable fixed-attachment lesson on the accepted M2 Max product. It does not prove fracture mechanics, material failure, deformation, liquid slosh, sound, cross-platform support, production readiness or arbitrary photoreal filmmaking.
stopRule: Retain the attempt as FAIL if the cap does not remain attached before contact, does not detach within the frozen post-contact window, teleports, fails to settle, violates any authority or regression check, or receives any direct visual NO. Correct only a reusable schema, factory, constraint, measurement, persistence or camera rule in a versioned contract; never hand-place the observed break or final pose.
